Dana — thanks for the clear note and the workbook. High level answer: our standard practice is that packaging credits are applied as invoice-level adjustments after usage-based billing is calculated; they are not deducted from the committed floor used to determine whether a true-up is triggered. That said, customers commonly negotiate the opposite (credits reduce the floor) for consolidated SKUs or migration credits, and we can accommodate that with explicit language in the order schedule.

To help move this forward I pasted two short options below and attached a tracked redline to Exhibit B so legal can confirm exact wording. Please tell us which you'd prefer and we'll issue final language.

Option A — Credits applied post-billing (default):
- Usage & committed floor are calculated on gross usage.
- Packaging credits are issued as invoice adjustments applied after the floor assessment.
- True-up calculations use pre-credit floor numbers; credits do not reduce the floor.

Option B — Credits reduce floor (customer-favorable):
- Packaging credits are netted against usage before floor assessment.
- The net usage is used to determine whether the committed floor was met; true-ups reflect neted amounts.

Proposal / next steps:
1) We can accept Option B for Acme if you confirm in writing; we'll prepare a one-paragraph amendment to Exhibit B that explicitly states credits reduce floor for consolidated SKUs.
2) Legal (cc'd) will provide redline language for the order schedule.
3) Ops (Marissa) will outline billing flow and expected invoice impact.

I've attached a preliminary redline: pricing_exhibit_redline_v1.pdf (draft). Let me know if you'd like a call — happy to jump on 20 minutes to lock this down.

Best,
Karthik Iyer

Legal redline (Option A - standard):
